key_insight: CRISP improves medical image segmentation under domain shift by using stable probability rankings to build robust spatial priors without needing target-domain data or test-time updates.
clinical_relevance: This could make segmentation models more reliable across hospitals, patient groups, and imaging modalities, helping reduce performance drops in real-world deployment.
method: Assumes rank stability of positive regions under distribution shift to extract robust spatial hints.
Uses latent feature perturbations to form a high-precision core and a high-recall support region.
Iteratively trains the model to progressively squeeze these priors toward the final segmentation mask.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong robustness gains on multi-center cardiac MRI and CT lung vessel segmentation, with HD95 reductions up to 0.14, 1.90, and 8.39 pixels across different shift types.
watch_item: The approach relies on the rank-stability assumption, so performance may depend on how well that assumption holds for new diseases, scanners, or segmentation tasks.
paper_title: CRISP: Constrained Refinement via Iterative Squeezing Process for Robust Medical Image Segmentation under Domain Shift
